title: JANUS Face Microcontrol Learning Update v2.2 — Verify the Coordinate System, Preserve Platform Failures, and Bind External Evidence to Current Authorization

new_lessons.learning: The first Windows gate found a real SQLite handle-lifetime defect that Linux tolerated. A second operating system is therefore an adversarial verifier of resource ownership and cleanup semantics, not cosmetic compatibility work.

Syntactic resource patterns must not be mistaken for lifecycle guarantees. sqlite3.Connection context management controls transactions but does not close the connection; JANUS now records resource ownership as part of correctness.
Verifying reviewer lineages is insufficient if the origin can self-declare a different root. Independence must be computed in a coordinate system whose origin is itself evidence-bound.

A signature proves binding to a configured issuer/key, not objective genealogy. JANUS may use a reference HMAC attestation to test the boundary while keeping real issuer truth, rotation, revocation, and expiry outside the claim ceiling.
Provider/effect/idempotency identity alone is not enough across reauthorization. Evidence that was valid for AUTH-OLD must not silently clear uncertainty for AUTH-NEW.
Even a nominally read-only external lookup is an external action boundary. Obvious adapter/provider mismatch should be rejected before the call rather than detected after unnecessary contact.
Stable request identity prevents intent substitution; immutable settlement prevents outcome substitution. They are separate controls and both are required.

If a client request is already settled, a generic executor must not call the world again just to reproduce an answer. Without a replayable full result envelope, the safe client-boundary behavior is fail-closed and expose the settlement hash/state.

The client ledger can preserve request identity but cannot manufacture exactly-once execution. A crash after binding and before outer settlement still depends on the lower controlled runtime's receipt/UNDETERMINED semantics.

The Windows v18.7.28 failure remains explicitly linked from the v18.7.29/v18.7.30 success lineage. A corrected descendant proves the correction; it does not turn the earlier implementation into something that had passed.

epistemic_upgrade.before: v2.1 protected unknown across request identity, crash boundaries, lineage-count review, and provider lookup identity
epistemic_upgrade.after: v2.2 additionally protects the origin coordinate system, authorization lineage, resource lifetime across operating systems, and settlement immutability
epistemic_upgrade.formula: VERIFIED_COORDINATE_SYSTEM > SELF_DECLARED_ROOT; CURRENT_AUTHORIZATION_EVIDENCE > STALE_SIGNED_EVIDENCE; IMMUTABLE_SETTLEMENT > REEXECUTION; CROSS_PLATFORM_FAILURE > ASSUMED_PORTABILITY

next_learning_question: Can JANUS migrate the historical POSIX-only control chain to portable locks, route the default CLI through explicit persistent request identities without conflating repeated identical actions, make session-store replacement crash-durable, and add real key lifecycle/revocation semantics while preserving every old failed verifier and implementation run?
